summaryBox.title: CIP Rules
summaryBox.takeaway: Higher atomic number = higher priority. Z-isomer = higher priority on same side; E-isomer = opposite sides.

conceptBreakdown.codeSnippet:
GEOMETRICAL ISOMERISM (E/Z)
                                       │
   Cahn-Ingold-Prelog (CIP) Priority Rules ──► Assign priority by Atomic Number (Z)
                                       │
   ┌───────────────────────────────────┴───────────────────────────────────┐
   ▼                                                                       ▼
   Z-ISOMER (Zusammen = Together)                                          E-ISOMER (Entgegen = Opposite)
   Higher priority groups on SAME SIDE of C=C.                             Higher priority groups on OPPOSITE SIDES.
conceptBreakdown.content:
• **CIP Priority Rules**: Priority is assigned based on atomic number ($Z$) of the atom directly attached to the $sp^2$ carbon ($-\text{I} > -\text{Br} > -\text{Cl} > -\text{OH} > -\text{NH}_2 > -\text{CH}_3 > -\text{H}$).
• **$Z$-Isomer (*Zusammen*)**: Both high-priority groups on the same side of the double bond.
• **$E$-Isomer (*Entgegen*)**: High-priority groups on opposite sides.

conceptBreakdown.heading: 3.2 Elimination Regioselectivity: Saytzeff vs. Hofmann
conceptBreakdown.title: 3.2 Elimination Regioselectivity: Saytzeff vs. Hofmann
conceptBreakdown.codeSnippet:
ELIMINATION REGIOSELECTIVITY RULES

• Saytzeff (Zaitsev) Rule: Major product is the more substituted, thermodynamically stable alkene (more α-H). Favored by good leaving groups (I⁻, Br⁻, Cl⁻) and unhindered bases (EtO⁻, OH⁻).
• Hofmann Rule: Major product is the less substituted, least hindered alkene. Favored by bulky bases (t-BuO⁻) or poor leaving groups (-N⁺R₃, F⁻).
conceptBreakdown.content: Dehydrohalogenation ($E2$) regioselectivity depends on base size and leaving group character. Bulky bases like Potassium tert-butoxide ($t\text{-BuOK}$) cannot easily abstract sterically hindered internal protons, forcing elimination of terminal protons to give the **Hofmann product**.

quickRevision: Z = high priority on same side; E = opposite sides.
Saytzeff gives the more substituted alkene (more α-H).
Hofmann gives the less substituted alkene (bulky bases).
